drhp.business: Bajel Projects Limited provides engineering, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning services across power transmission, new energies, monopoles, and emerging adjacencies like data centers and battery storage. The company serves utilities, transmission developers, and industrial clients in India and select international markets, leveraging its Ranjangaon manufacturing facility for backward integration. It operates as a distinct listed entity following its demerger from Bajaj Electricals Limited in 2023, drawing on the governance standards of the Bajaj Group.
drhp.end_markets: India (domestic power T&D, urban infrastructure, industrial power)|Select African markets (EPC projects)|More than seven countries (product supply)|Saudi Arabia (via 50:50 JV for HV/EHV EPC)
drhp.expansion: During FY26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of ₹37.56 crore, primarily towards property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and other intangible assets. As of March 31, 2026, gross fixed assets stood at ₹195.43 crore. The Company continues to focus on judicious management of working capital and cash flows to support its business requirements. No specific new capacity expansion projects with commissioning timelines were disclosed.

litigation.note: No material litigation disclosed in the provided annual report sections.

drhp.one_liner: Bajel Projects Limited is a Bajaj Group power infrastructure EPC specialist with over two decades of experience, executing high-voltage transmission, monopole, and emerging energy projects while pivoting toward quality-of-earnings and scalable growth under its RAASTA 2030 strategy.

risks.note: As a power transmission and distribution EPC company, delays, cost overruns, or quality issues on complex projects can materially impact profitability and reputation.
risks.risk: Execution and project delivery risk in large-scale EPC contracts

risks.note: Revenue concentration with key customers or regions exposes the company to significant financial impact if a major client delays or cancels orders.
risks.risk: Concentration risk from dependence on a limited number of large clients or geographies

risks.note: The business requires substantial working capital for inventories and receivables; any strain on cash flows or tightening of credit could constrain operations and growth.
risks.risk: Working capital intensity and liquidity risk

risks.note: Changes in government policies, tariff regulations, or delayed approvals for power transmission projects can adversely affect order inflow and project execution.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk in the power sector

risks.note: Intense competition in the EPC space may lead to aggressive bidding, compressing margins and making it difficult to secure profitable orders.
The company relies on a small senior management team; the departure of key executives (e.g., CFO change in 2025, CS/Compliance Officer change in 2026) could disrupt strategic continuity.
Fluctuations in prices of steel, copper, and other inputs can erode project margins, especially for fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses.
risks.risk: Supply chain and raw material price volatility

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
